<issue identifier="MM-355">
<title>Migration identity-leg submit: reconcile ambiguous/lost-response PLC submit before retry</title>
<description>
## Problem

The outbound-migration identity-leg submit (`migrate::submit_migration_op_cmd`) is not resilient to an **ambiguous / lost-response** PLC submission. Because a PLC operation is `prev`-chained and non-idempotent, `submit_migration_op_cmd` `.take()`s the signed op under the lock (to prevent a double-POST) and clears `migration_state` only *after* a confirmed 200.

If [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) commits the op but the HTTP response is lost (mobile network drop), the wallet lands in a dead-end state:

* `migration_state = Some { signed_op: None }` (op was taken, but state not cleared because no success was observed).
* The frontend (`MigrationReviewScreen.svelte`) sees a transport error, so its `submitted` flag stays `false`.
* On retry, `approve()` re-calls `submitMigrationOp` → `submit_migration_op_cmd` finds `signed_op == None` → returns terminal `MIGRATION_NOT_READY` ("no signed op; build the migration operation first").
* `finalizeMigration` also can't proceed: its gate requires `migration_state == None`, but it's `Some`.

The account is **not** broken (the source is still active and the identity op did land, so the DID points at the destination), but the in-app migration is stranded and needs manual recovery.

This is **pre-existing** (the pre-<issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue> `approve()` had the same re-submit-on-retry behavior) and is upstream of the <issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue> cutover, so it was deliberately left out of that PR (see <pull-request id="3505a4f2-76ee-49d6-a809-2de4d00f96dc" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/review/featwallet-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source-66d203513560">malpercio-dev/ezpds#235</pull-request> — CodeRabbit thread on `MigrationReviewScreen.svelte`).

## Proposed fix

Reconcile the identity op's landed-state before deciding to re-submit vs. proceed:

* On a submit failure (or on entry to `submit_migration_op_cmd` with an already-taken `signed_op`), fetch the DID's PLC audit log and check whether the migration op already landed (current `atproto_pds` service == destination, or the latest non-nullified op matches the built op).
* If **landed** → clear `migration_state`, return the equivalent `ClaimResult`, and let the flow continue to `finalizeMigration` (which is now idempotent per <issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue>).
* If **not landed** → the op can be safely rebuilt (`build_migration_op`) and re-submitted, since `prev` is unchanged.
* Wire the frontend retry to this reconciliation rather than blindly re-invoking `submitMigrationOp`.

Sibling to <issue id="91456924-d043-4164-baa8-112e1ff1e865" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-299/migration-mode-createaccount-is-not-resumable-a-mid-flight-failure">MM-299</issue> (migration-mode createAccount resumability). Add mock tests for the landed/not-landed reconciliation branches.

## Non-goals

* No change to the <issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue> cutover ordering (activate → sovereign session → persist → deactivate → Finalized), which already handles its own idempotent retry.
</description>

<title>Sovereign passwordless login — mint a Custos session from a device-key signature over the DID's rotation set (migrated accounts have no password by design)</title>
<description>
## Outcome

A managed identity hosted by Custos can obtain and later renew a standard full-access session by proving control of a key in the DID's **current PLC rotation set**. Migrated accounts remain passwordless by design, and migration never deactivates the source until the destination credential is durable.

## Why

After outbound migration, the destination account has `password_hash = NULL`. Once the wallet's in-memory destination session is lost, full-access operations such as `updateHandle`, app-password management, email changes, PLC-operation requests, account deactivation, and agent management are unreachable. The concrete instance that exposed this was `did:plc:u7j7xdhvkwx3xlf6xjkbpdn7` during <issue id="10c8aa2a-f2fe-433f-9ba4-fed81b554e7a" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-241/validate-live-bskysocial-migration-round-trip-canonical-mm-207-e2e">MM-241</issue> leg (b).

A PLC rotation key is the identity-owner credential and is stronger than a password. Passwords remain optional break-glass credentials; migration must not collect one by default.

## Protocol decision

Use a one-request, timestamped proof at `POST /v1/sessions/sovereign`, rather than a stored two-step challenge.

The wallet signs one canonical, domain-separated envelope binding the destination server DID, method/path, account DID, signing-key DID, timestamp, and random nonce. Custos:

1. requires a locally hosted active account;
2. reads the latest non-nullified PLC audit-log operation from [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>);
3. requires the signing key in that operation's `rotationKeys`;
4. verifies the curve-appropriate signature;
5. atomically consumes DID + nonce within a bounded timestamp window;
6. issues the same full-access access/refresh session as password `createSession`.

The authoritative rotation set comes from PLC operation state, **not** the cached W3C DID document, which does not reliably expose `rotationKeys`. Any current rotation key qualifies under PLC semantics, including a Custos-held rotation key; that grants Custos no new power over data it already hosts.

## Child issues

1. <issue id="2b2651ac-c6a4-4374-80f0-323be617de6d" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-350/sovereign-sessions-reusable-full-access-session-issuer-and-replay">MM-350</issue> **— server foundation:** reusable full-session issuer plus dedicated sovereign replay persistence/sweeping.
2. <issue id="25aa82ae-c063-4c30-afb1-bd8d65182211" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-351/custos-post-v1sessionssovereign-with-current-plc-rotation-key">MM-351</issue> **— verified endpoint:** current PLC rotation-set lookup, dual-curve signature verification, rate limiting, route/Bruno contract, and integration tests. Blocked by <issue id="2b2651ac-c6a4-4374-80f0-323be617de6d" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-350/sovereign-sessions-reusable-full-access-session-issuer-and-replay">MM-350</issue>.
3. <issue id="79f7ec05-e3d8-4682-bdd9-cf2f190664af" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-352/wallet-per-did-sovereign-login-client-and-keychain-session-persistence">MM-352</issue> **— wallet credential plumbing:** per-DID signed client, versioned `oauth-tokens` Keychain storage, Bearer-client construction, and biometric-gated IPC. Blocked by <issue id="25aa82ae-c063-4c30-afb1-bd8d65182211" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-351/custos-post-v1sessionssovereign-with-current-plc-rotation-key">MM-351</issue>.
4. <issue id="adcfe489-abaf-4914-b2c6-2d89472dd9b7" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-353/wallet-restore-refresh-and-passwordlessly-renew-per-identity-custos">MM-353</issue> **— session lifecycle:** restore, refresh, coalesce, and passwordlessly renew per-identity sessions after restart. This is the child that directly unblocks <issue id="c41f0839-9de0-4215-be44-c94a5267f033" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-305/wallet-change-handle-flow-wallet-signed-alsoknownas-plc-op">MM-305</issue>. Blocked by <issue id="79f7ec05-e3d8-4682-bdd9-cf2f190664af" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-352/wallet-per-did-sovereign-login-client-and-keychain-session-persistence">MM-352</issue>.
5. <issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue> **— safe migration cutover:** activate destination → sovereign login → persist → deactivate source → Finalized, with retry/crash ordering tests. Blocked by <issue id="79f7ec05-e3d8-4682-bdd9-cf2f190664af" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-352/wallet-per-did-sovereign-login-client-and-keychain-session-persistence">MM-352</issue>.

## Delivery order

`MM-350 → MM-351 → MM-352 → { MM-353, MM-354 }`

<issue id="adcfe489-abaf-4914-b2c6-2d89472dd9b7" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-353/wallet-restore-refresh-and-passwordlessly-renew-per-identity-custos">MM-353</issue> and <issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue> can proceed independently once the wallet client/storage contract exists.

## Definition of done

* Current P-256 and secp256k1 PLC rotation keys can mint a full session; fossil/non-rotation keys cannot.
* Replay, cross-PDS replay, stale/future timestamp, inactive-account, and [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) failure paths fail closed.
* Per-DID tokens survive app restart, refresh safely, and never cross identities/PDS audiences.
* Biometric cancellation signs/sends nothing.
* Migration persists the destination credential before touching the source account.
* A restarted wallet can perform a full-access operation for the migrated DID with no password.
* <issue id="c41f0839-9de0-4215-be44-c94a5267f033" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-305/wallet-change-handle-flow-wallet-signed-alsoknownas-plc-op">MM-305</issue> is unblocked.

## Related work

* <issue id="6a949579-cfaf-4f69-b1b6-a02777c3775f" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-304/verify-service-auth-jwt-rejects-es256k-bsky-minted-createaccount">MM-304</issue> supplied the reusable dual-curve verification pattern.
* <issue id="91456924-d043-4164-baa8-112e1ff1e865" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-299/migration-mode-createaccount-is-not-resumable-a-mid-flight-failure">MM-299</issue> made migration-mode destination account creation resumable.
* <issue id="236f7ee6-538c-460b-8055-d97e34a54b26" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-302/outbound-migration-source-login-must-be-a-full-session-bsky-refuses">MM-302</issue> established why the source migration login still needs a full session on reference PDSes.
* <issue id="586111c2-5b25-4759-947b-214560b6bb5b" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-309/operator-account-repair-ops-for-the-brass-console-correct-email-issue">MM-309</issue> remains the separate operator break-glass/account-repair surface.
</description>

3. <issue id="79f7ec05-e3d8-4682-bdd9-cf2f190664af" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-352/wallet-per-did-sovereign-login-client-and-keychain-session-persistence">MM-352</issue> **— wallet credential plumbing:** per-DID signed client, versioned `oauth-tokens` Keychain storage, Bearer-client construction, and biometric-gated IPC. Blocked by <issue id="25aa82ae-c063-4c30-afb1-bd8d65182211" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-351/custos-post-v1sessionssovereign-with-current-plc-rotation-key">MM-351</issue>.
4. <issue id="adcfe489-abaf-4914-b2c6-2d89472dd9b7" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-353/wallet-restore-refresh-and-passwordlessly-renew-per-identity-custos">MM-353</issue> **— session lifecycle:** restore, refresh, coalesce, and passwordlessly renew per-identity sessions after restart. This is the child that directly unblocks <issue id="c41f0839-9de0-4215-be44-c94a5267f033" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-305/wallet-change-handle-flow-wallet-signed-alsoknownas-plc-op">MM-305</issue>. Blocked by <issue id="79f7ec05-e3d8-4682-bdd9-cf2f190664af" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-352/wallet-per-did-sovereign-login-client-and-keychain-session-persistence">MM-352</issue>.
5. <issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue> **— safe migration cutover:** activate destination → sovereign login → persist → deactivate source → Finalized, with retry/crash ordering tests. Blocked by <issue id="79f7ec05-e3d8-4682-bdd9-cf2f190664af" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-352/wallet-per-did-sovereign-login-client-and-keychain-session-persistence">MM-352</issue>.

## Delivery order

`MM-350 → MM-351 → MM-352 → { MM-353, MM-354 }`

<issue id="adcfe489-abaf-4914-b2c6-2d89472dd9b7" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-353/wallet-restore-refresh-and-passwordlessly-renew-per-identity-custos">MM-353</issue> and <issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue> can proceed independently once the wallet client/storage contract exists.

## Definition of done

* Current P-256 and secp256k1 PLC rotation keys can mint a full session; fossil/non-rotation keys cannot.
* Replay, cross-PDS replay, stale/future timestamp, inactive-account, and [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) failure paths fail closed.
* Per-DID tokens survive app restart, refresh safely, and never cross identities/PDS audiences.
* Biometric cancellation signs/sends nothing.
* Migration persists the destination credential before touching the source account.
* A restarted wallet can perform a full-access operation for the migrated DID with no password.
* <issue id="c41f0839-9de0-4215-be44-c94a5267f033" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-305/wallet-change-handle-flow-wallet-signed-alsoknownas-plc-op">MM-305</issue> is unblocked.

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

{"id":"MM-355","title":"Migration identity-leg submit: reconcile ambiguous/lost-response PLC submit before retry","description":"## Problem

The outbound-migration identity-leg submit (`migrate::submit_migration_op_cmd`) is not resilient to an **ambiguous / lost-response** PLC submission. Because a PLC operation is `prev`-chained and non-idempotent, `submit_migration_op_cmd` `.take()`s the signed op under the lock (to prevent a double-POST) and clears `migration_state` only *after* a confirmed 200.

If [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) commits the op but the HTTP response is lost (mobile network drop), the wallet lands in a dead-end state:

* `migration_state = Some { signed_op: None }` (op was taken, but state not cleared because no success was observed).
* The frontend (`MigrationReviewScreen.svelte`) sees a transport error, so its `submitted` flag stays `false`.
* On retry, `approve()` re-calls `submitMigrationOp` → `submit_migration_op_cmd` finds `signed_op == None` → returns terminal `MIGRATION_NOT_READY` ("no signed op; build the migration operation first").
* `finalizeMigration` also can't proceed: its gate requires `migration_state == None`, but it's `Some`.

The account is **not** broken (the source is still active and the identity op did land, so the DID points at the destination), but the in-app migration is stranded and needs manual recovery.

This is **pre-existing** (the pre-<issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue> `approve()` had the same re-submit-on-retry behavior) and is upstream of the <issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue> cutover, so it was deliberately left out of that PR (see <pull-request id="3505a4f2-76ee-49d6-a809-2de4d00f96dc" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/review/featwallet-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source-66d203513560">malpercio-dev/ezpds#235</pull-request> — CodeRabbit thread on `MigrationReviewScreen.svelte`).

## Proposed fix

Reconcile the identity op's landed-state before deciding to re-submit vs. proceed:

{"id":"MM-355","title":"Migration identity-leg submit: reconcile ambiguous/lost-response PLC submit before retry","description":"## Problem

The outbound-migration identity-leg submit (`migrate::submit_migration_op_cmd`) is not resilient to an **ambiguous / lost-response** PLC submission. Because a PLC operation is `prev`-chained and non-idempotent, `submit_migration_op_cmd` `.take()`s the signed op under the lock (to prevent a double-POST) and clears `migration_state` only *after* a confirmed 200.

If [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) commits the op but the HTTP response is lost (mobile network drop), the wallet lands in a dead-end state:

* `migration_state = Some { signed_op: None }` (op was taken, but state not cleared because no success was observed).
* The frontend (`MigrationReviewScreen.svelte`) sees a transport error, so its `submitted` flag stays `false`.
* On retry, `approve()` re-calls `submitMigrationOp` → `submit_migration_op_cmd` finds `signed_op == None` → returns terminal `MIGRATION_NOT_READY` ("no signed op; build the migration operation first").
* `finalizeMigration` also can't proceed: its gate requires `migration_state == None`, but it's `Some`.

The account is **not** broken (the source is still active and the identity op did land, so the DID points at the destination), but the in-app migration is stranded and needs manual recovery.

This is **pre-existing** (the pre-<issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue> `approve()` had the same re-submit-on-retry behavior) and is upstream of the <issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue> cutover, so it was deliberately left out of that PR (see <pull-request id="3505a4f2-76ee-49d6-a809-2de4d00f96dc" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/review/featwallet-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source-66d203513560">malpercio-dev/ezpds#235</pull-request> — CodeRabbit thread on `MigrationReviewScreen.svelte`).

23	/// Migration phase tracking the outbound migration flow.
24	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize)]
25	pub enum MigrationPhase {
26	    Resolved,
27	    SourceAuthed,
28	    DestCreated,
29	    RepoTransferred,
30	    BlobsTransferred,
31	    PreferencesTransferred,
32	    Verified,
33	    IdentityArmed,

35	}

38	
39	/// Outbound migration state persisted in `AppState`.
40	///
41	/// Resolved by `prepare_migration` and used by subsequent migration commands
42	/// within the same migration session. In-memory only; an app kill restarts from
43	/// `prepare_migration`.
44	#[derive(Clone)]
45	pub struct OutboundMigrationState {
46	    /// The DID being migrated
47	    pub did: String,
48	    /// Source PDS URL (resolved by `prepare_migration` via `discover_pds`)
49	    pub source_pds_url: String,
50	    /// Destination PDS URL (provided by caller to `prepare_migration`)
51	    pub dest_pds_url: String,
52	    /// Destination server DID (from `describeServer`, used as `aud` for `getServiceAuth`)
53	    pub dest_did: String,
54	    /// Handle (preserved from source; extracted from `plc_doc.also_known_as`)
55	    pub handle: String,
56	    /// Full-session Bearer client for the source PDS (set after `authenticate_migration_source`).
57	    /// Wrapped in Arc to allow cloning out of the Mutex without holding the lock
58	    /// across network calls.
59	    pub source_client: Option<Arc<OAuthClient>>,
60	    /// OAuth client for destination PDS (set after `create_destination_account`)
61	    /// Wrapped in Arc to allow cloning out of the Mutex without holding the lock
62	    /// across network calls.
63	    pub dest_client: Option<Arc<OAuthClient>>,
64	    /// Current phase in the migration flow
65	    pub phase: MigrationPhase,
66	}
67	
68	/// Resolved source identity returned by `prepare_migration`, so the source-auth screen can prefill
69	/// the login identifier and show which PDS it is signing into (mirrors the claim flow's
70	/// `IdentityInfo`). The authoritative `source_pds_url` used for the actual `createSession` lives in
71	/// `OutboundMigrationState` — this copy is display/prefill only.
72	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
73	#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
74	pub struct PreparedMigration {
75	    /// Handle of the identity being migrated (from the source DID doc's `alsoKnownAs`).
76	    pub handle: String,
77	    /// Source PDS base URL (the account's current PDS, resolved via `discover_pds`).

79	}

81	// ── Error types ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
82	
83	/// Error returned by outbound migration commands.
84	///
85	/// Serializes as `{ "code": "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` matching the wallet's
86	/// established error contract (same pattern as `ClaimError`, `CreateAccountError`).
87	#[derive(Debug, Serialize, thiserror::Error)]
88	#[serde(tag = "code", rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE")]
89	pub enum MigrationError {
90	    /// Migration not ready: state absent, DID mismatch, or phase too low
91	    #[error("migration not ready: {message}")]
92	    MigrationNotReady { message: String },
93	    /// Destination PDS is unreachable
94	    #[error("destination unreachable: {message}")]
95	    DestinationUnreachable { message: String },
96	    /// The source PDS rejected the password login (`createSession` 401). Distinct from a network
97	    /// failure so the UI can say "wrong password" instead of blaming the connection. An app
98	    /// password is a lesser scope and is refused the same way.
99	    #[error("source auth failed: {message}")]
100	    SourceAuthFailed { message: String },
101	    /// The source account has email two-factor enabled: `createSession` returned
102	    /// `AuthFactorTokenRequired` and the PDS emailed a one-time code. The UI prompts for the code
103	    /// and re-invokes `authenticate_migration_source` with it — distinct from a wrong password.
104	    #[error("two-factor code required")]
105	    TwoFactorRequired,
106	    /// The source PDS session is for a different account than the one being migrated (the entered
107	    /// credentials signed in to the wrong account). Refused before any migration step proceeds.
108	    #[error("account mismatch")]
109	    AccountMismatch,
110	    /// Refused to send the account password to a non-HTTPS source PDS (loopback excepted). The PDS
111	    /// endpoint comes from the DID document, so a plaintext `http://` endpoint is rejected.
112	    #[error("insecure source url")]
113	    InsecureSourceUrl,
114	    /// The source PDS rate-limited the login (HTTP 429). `retry_after` carries the server's
115	    /// `Retry-After` value when present, so the UI can say how long to wait rather than blaming the
116	    /// connection.
117	    #[error("rate limited")]
118	    RateLimited {
119	        #[serde(rename = "retryAfter")]
120	        retry_after: Option<String>,
121	    },
122	    /// The source PDS rejected the login with a non-2xx the wallet doesn't model specially.
123	    /// `message` is the server's own error text, shown verbatim so a third-party PDS's real reason
124	    /// reaches the user instead of connectivity boilerplate.
125	    #[error("server error: {message}")]
126	    ServerError { message: String },
127	    /// Service authentication (getServiceAuth) failed
128	    #[error("service auth failed: {message}")]
129	    ServiceAuthFailed { message: String },
130	    /// Account creation (createAccount) failed
131	    #[error("account creation failed: {message}")]
132	    AccountCreationFailed { message: String },
133	    /// Destination account exists but session was lost (app kill; restart migration)
134	    #[error("destination conflict: {message}")]
135	    DestinationConflict { message: String },
136	    /// Repository transfer failed
137	    #[error("repo transfer failed: {message}")]
138	    RepoTransferFailed { message: String },
139	    /// Blob transfer failed
140	    #[error("blob transfer failed: {message}")]
141	    BlobTransferFailed { message: String },
142	    /// Preferences transfer failed
143	    #[error("preferences transfer failed: {message}")]
144	    PreferencesTransferFailed { message: String },
145	    /// Verification incomplete: imported entries do not match expected count
146	    #[error("verification incomplete")]
147	    VerificationIncomplete { imported: u64, expected: u64 },
148	    /// Identity activation failed
149	    #[error("activation failed: {message}")]
150	    ActivationFailed { message: String },
151	    /// Minting the destination sovereign session failed (device-key proof rejected, rate limited,
152	    /// server error, or transport failure). A retryable *pre-cutover* failure: the source account
153	    /// is still active and the migration can be retried. Never advances to `Finalized`.
154	    #[error("sovereign login failed: {message}")]
155	    SovereignLoginFailed { message: String },
156	    /// Persisting the destination sovereign session to the Keychain failed. Retryable pre-cutover
157	    /// failure — the source stays active and the migration can be retried. The prior valid token
158	    /// record (if any) is left intact because the write is atomic (replace-or-fail).
159	    #[error("session persist failed: {message}")]
160	    SessionPersistFailed { message: String },
161	    /// Account deactivation failed
162	    #[error("deactivation failed: {message}")]
163	    DeactivationFailed { message: String },
164	    /// Network error during migration
165	    #[error("network error: {message}")]
166	    NetworkError { message: String },

169	// ── Pure prerequisite gate ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
170	
171	/// Pure prerequisite gate: state present, DID matches, and phase is at least `required`.
172	/// No network, no side effects — this is what makes the gate side-effect-free and
173	/// unit-testable.
174	pub(crate) fn ensure_phase_did<'a>(
175	    state: &'a Option<OutboundMigrationState>,
176	    did: &str,
177	    required: MigrationPhase,
178	) -> Result<&'a OutboundMigrationState, MigrationError> {
179	    let Some(s) = state.as_ref() else {
180	        return Err(MigrationError::MigrationNotReady {
181	            message: "no migration in progress".into(),
182	        });
183	    };
184	    if s.did != did {
185	        return Err(MigrationError::MigrationNotReady {
186	            message: "did does not match active migration".into(),
187	        });
188	    }
189	    if s.phase < required {
190	        return Err(MigrationError::MigrationNotReady {
191	            message: format!("expected phase >= {:?}, found {:?}", required, s.phase),
192	        });
193	    }
194	    Ok(s)
195	}
196	
197	// ── Task 4: prepare_migration ──────────────────────────────────────────────
198	
199	/// Resolve destination + source PDS and store migration state at phase Resolved.
200	///
201	/// 1. discover_pds(did) → source_pds_url + handle (from also_known_as, strip "at://")
202	/// 2. describe_server(dest_pds_url) → dest_did (map PdsUnreachable → DESTINATION_UNREACHABLE)
203	/// 3. store fresh OutboundMigrationState at phase Resolved (in-memory only; app kill restarts)
204	#[tauri::command]
205	pub async fn prepare_migration(
206	    state: tauri::State<'_, crate::oauth::AppState>,
207	    did: String,
208	    dest_pds_url: String,
209	) -> Result<PreparedMigration, MigrationError> {
210	    let result = prepare_migration_impl(state.pds_client(), &did, &dest_pds_url).await?;
211	
212	    // Surface the resolved source identity so the source-auth screen can prefill the login
213	    // identifier and show which PDS it is signing into (the authoritative copy stays in state).
214	    let prepared = PreparedMigration {
215	        handle: result.handle.clone(),
216	        source_pds_url: result.source_pds_url.clone(),
217	    };
218	
219	    // Store fresh state at phase Resolved (in-memory only; app kill restarts from prepare_migration)
220	    *state.orchestration_state.lock().await = Some(result);
221	    Ok(prepared)
222	}
223	
224	/// Pure core: discover source + dest, return fresh OutboundMigrationState at Resolved.
225	async fn prepare_migration_impl(
226	    pds_client: &crate::pds_client::PdsClient,
227	    did: &str,
228	    dest_pds_url: &str,
229	) -> Result<OutboundMigrationState, MigrationError> {
230	    tracing::info!(did = %did, dest_url = %dest_pds_url, "prepare_migration: discovering source + destination");
231	
232	    // 1. Discover source PDS
233	    let (source_pds_url, plc_doc) = pds_client.discover_pds(did).await.map_err(|e| {
234	        tracing::error!(did = %did, error = %e, "failed to discover source PDS");
235	        // Preserve the unreachable distinction in the message (there is no SourceUnreachable
236	        // variant; only the destination is named, but a bare NetworkError is less actionable).
237	        match e {
238	            crate::pds_client::PdsClientError::PdsUnreachable { .. } => {
239	                MigrationError::NetworkError {
240	                    message: format!("source PDS unreachable: {}", e),
241	                }
242	            }
243	            other => MigrationError::NetworkError {
244	                message: format!("source discovery failed: {}", other),
245	            },
246	        }
247	    })?;
248	
249	    // Extract handle from also_known_as (format: at://handle). A DID document with no at:// entry
250	    // is a data problem (unusable identity), not a network error — surface it as such.
251	    let handle = extract_handle_from_also_known_as(&plc_doc.also_known_as).ok_or_else(|| {
252	        tracing::error!(did = %did, "no at:// handle in also_known_as");
253	        MigrationError::AccountCreationFailed {
254	            message: "source DID document has no at:// handle in alsoKnownAs".into(),
255	        }
256	    })?;
257	
258	    // 2. Describe destination server
259	    let dest_describe = pds_client
260	        .describe_server(dest_pds_url)
261	        .await
262	        .map_err(|e| {
263	            tracing::error!(dest_url = %dest_pds_url, error = %e, "describe_server failed");
264	            match e {
265	                crate::pds_client::PdsClientError::PdsUnreachable { .. } => {
266	                    MigrationError::DestinationUnreachable {
267	                        message: format!("destination unreachable: {}", e),
268	                    }
269	                }
270	                other => MigrationError::NetworkError {
271	                    message: format!("describe_server failed: {}", other),
272	                },
273	            }
274	        })?;
275	
276	    tracing::info!(
277	        source_url = %source_pds_url,
278	        dest_url = %dest_pds_url,
279	        dest_did = %dest_describe.did,
280	        handle = %handle,
281	        "migration resolved"
282	    );
283	
284	    // 3. Build fresh state at Resolved phase
285	    Ok(OutboundMigrationState {
286	        did: did.to_string(),
287	        source_pds_url,
288	        dest_pds_url: dest_pds_url.to_string(),
289	        dest_did: dest_describe.did,
290	        handle,
291	        source_client: None,
292	        dest_client: None,
293	        phase: MigrationPhase::Resolved,
294	    })
295	}
296	
297	// ── Task 5: Source-PDS password login ──────────────────────────────────────
298	
299	/// Authenticate with the source PDS using the account **password** (`createSession`), yielding a
300	/// full-session Bearer client that the migration then uses for its source-side calls.
301	///
302	/// Why a password and not the wallet's OAuth token: creating the destination account
303	/// (`create_destination_account`) mints a `com.atproto.server.createAccount` service-auth token
304	/// **from the source PDS**, and a spec-strict PDS such as bsky.social gates that mint behind a full
305	/// session — an OAuth `transition:generic` grant is refused (`insufficient access`). A
306	/// password `createSession` mints a full `com.atproto.access` session, the only credential class
307	/// that can. This mirrors the claim flow's `authenticate_source_pds` (ADR-0021) — one password
308	/// path for every source login.
309	///
310	/// The password is used for exactly one `createSession` request and is never stored — the wallet
311	/// keeps only the resulting Bearer session, in memory, in `OutboundMigrationState.source_client`.
312	/// An app password is a lesser scope and is rejected the same way a wrong real password is.
313	///
314	/// `auth_factor_token` is the email 2FA one-time code. Pass `None` first; if the account has email
315	/// two-factor enabled the call returns `TwoFactorRequired` (and the PDS emails a code), and the UI
316	/// re-invokes with that code as `Some`.
317	///
318	/// Gate: `ensure_phase_did(..., Resolved)` — `prepare_migration` must have resolved the source PDS.
319	#[tauri::command]
320	pub async fn authenticate_migration_source(
321	    state: tauri::State<'_, crate::oauth::AppState>,
322	    did: String,
323	    identifier: String,
324	    password: String,
325	    auth_factor_token: Option<String>,
326	) -> Result<(), MigrationError> {
327	    tracing::info!(did = %did, "authenticate_migration_source: password login for source PDS");
328	
329	    // Snapshot the source PDS URL under the lock; the phase/DID gate is defense-in-depth.
330	    let source_pds_url = {
331	        let orchestration = state.orchestration_state.lock().await;
332	        let mig =
333	            ensure_phase_did(&orchestration, &did, MigrationPhase::Resolved).map_err(|e| {
334	                tracing::warn!("authenticate_migration_source: phase gate failed: {}", e);
335	                e
336	            })?;
337	        mig.source_pds_url.clone()
338	    }; // lock released — createSession is a network call
339	
340	    let oauth_client = authenticate_migration_source_impl(
341	        state.pds_client(),
342	        &source_pds_url,
343	        &did,
344	        &identifier,
345	        &password,
346	        auth_factor_token.as_deref(),
347	    )
348	    .await?;
349	
350	    // Re-acquire the lock and store the Bearer client, rejecting the write if a concurrent
351	    // `prepare_migration` swapped the active migration while we were on the network.
352	    let mut orchestration = state.orchestration_state.lock().await;
353	    match orchestration.as_mut() {
354	        Some(mig) if mig.did == did && mig.source_pds_url == source_pds_url => {
355	            mig.source_client = Some(std::sync::Arc::new(oauth_client));
356	            mig.phase = MigrationPhase::SourceAuthed;
357	            Ok(())
358	        }
359	        _ => {
360	            drop(orchestration);
361	            tracing::warn!("authenticate_migration_source: active migration changed during login");
362	            Err(MigrationError::MigrationNotReady {
363	                message: "migration state changed during source login".into(),
364	            })
365	        }
366	    }
367	}
368	
369	/// Testable core: run `createSession` against the source PDS and build a full-session Bearer
370	/// `OAuthClient`. Extracted so it can be exercised without Tauri's `State` wrapper (twin of
371	/// `claim::authenticate_source_pds_impl`).
372	///
373	/// `expected_did` is the DID being migrated: the session the PDS returns MUST be for that account,
374	/// or the caller signed in to the wrong one and we refuse to bind those credentials to this
375	/// migration.
376	pub(crate) async fn authenticate_migration_source_impl(
377	    pds_client: &crate::pds_client::PdsClient,
378	    source_pds_url: &str,
379	    expected_did: &str,
380	    identifier: &str,
381	    password: &str,

384	    let session = pds_client
385	        .create_session(source_pds_url, identifier, password, auth_factor_token)
386	        .await
387	        .map_err(|e| match e {
388	            crate::pds_client::PdsClientError::AuthFactorTokenRequired => {
389	                tracing::info!("source account has email 2FA; a code was sent");
390	                MigrationError::TwoFactorRequired
391	            }
392	            crate::pds_client::PdsClientError::InvalidCredentials { message } => {
393	                tracing::warn!(detail = %message, "source createSession rejected the password");
394	                MigrationError::SourceAuthFailed {
395	                    message: "The PDS did not accept that password.".to_string(),
396	                }
397	            }
398	            crate::pds_client::PdsClientError::InsecurePdsUrl { url } => {
399	                tracing::error!(pds_url = %url, "refusing password login to a non-HTTPS PDS");
400	                MigrationError::InsecureSourceUrl
401	            }
402	            // A rate limit or other server rejection during the password login must keep its real
403	            // reason too — a 429 here is not a connectivity problem.
404	            crate::pds_client::PdsClientError::RateLimited { retry_after, .. } => {
405	                MigrationError::RateLimited { retry_after }
406	            }
407	            crate::pds_client::PdsClientError::XrpcError { message, .. } => {
408	                MigrationError::ServerError { message }
409	            }
410	            other => MigrationError::NetworkError {
411	                message: format!("createSession failed: {}", other),
412	            },
413	        })?;
414	
415	    // The session must be for the account being migrated. A mismatch means the user signed in to a
416	    // different account (or a hostile PDS returned someone else's session) — refuse to bind those
417	    // credentials to this migration rather than transfer against the wrong identity.
418	    if session.did != expected_did {
419	        tracing::warn!(
420	            expected = %expected_did,
421	            got = %session.did,
422	            "source session DID does not match the migration"
423	        );
424	        return Err(MigrationError::AccountMismatch);
425	    }
426	
427	    OAuthClient::new_bearer(
428	        session.access_jwt,
429	        session.refresh_jwt,
430	        source_pds_url.to_string(),
431	    )
432	    .map_err(|e| {
433	        tracing::error!(error = %e, "failed to build Bearer client from source session");
434	        MigrationError::NetworkError {
435	            message: "failed to build source session client".to_string(),
436	        }
437	    })
438	}

441	
442	/// Pure core: reserve key, mint service-auth, create account, return Bearer client.
443	/// Extracted for unit testability with mocked servers.
444	// The explicit-dependency signature (source/dest clients, urls, dids, handle, email, invite,
445	// existing client) is deliberate for testability; a struct would only move the arity around.
446	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
447	async fn create_destination_account_impl(
448	    pds_client: &crate::pds_client::PdsClient,
449	    source_client: &Arc<OAuthClient>,
450	    dest_pds_url: &str,
451	    dest_did: &str,
452	    did: &str,
453	    handle: &str,
454	    email: &str,
455	    invite_code: Option<String>,
456	    existing_dest_client: Option<Arc<OAuthClient>>,
457	) -> Result<Arc<OAuthClient>, MigrationError> {
458	    // 0. Idempotent fast path: if dest_client already exists, return it.
459	    //    Borrow (don't move) so `existing_dest_client` survives to the DidAlreadyExists arm below.
460	    if let Some(client) = &existing_dest_client {
461	        tracing::info!(did = %did, "create_destination_account: dest_client exists, returning cached");
462	        return Ok(client.clone());
463	    }
464	
465	    // 1. Reserve signing key at destination
466	    tracing::debug!(did = %did, dest_url = %dest_pds_url, "reserving signing key at destination");
467	    let _reserved_key = pds_client
468	        .reserve_signing_key(dest_pds_url, did)
469	        .await
470	        .map_err(|e| {
471	            tracing::error!(did = %did, error = %e, "reserveSigningKey failed");
472	            MigrationError::AccountCreationFailed {
473	                message: format!("failed to reserve signing key: {}", e),
474	            }
475	        })?;
476	
477	    // 2. Get service auth token from source PDS
478	    tracing::debug!(did = %did, "getting service auth from source");
479	    let service_auth_token = crate::pds_client::get_service_auth(
480	        source_client,
481	        dest_did,
482	        "com.atproto.server.createAccount",
483	    )
484	    .await
485	    .map_err(|e| {
486	        tracing::error!(did = %did, error = %e, "getServiceAuth failed");
487	        MigrationError::ServiceAuthFailed {
488	            message: format!("failed to get service auth: {}", e),
489	        }
490	    })?;
491	
492	    // 3. One-shot Bearer client carrying the service-auth token
493	    let sa_client = OAuthClient::new_bearer(
494	        service_auth_token.token.clone(),
495	        String::new(),
496	        dest_pds_url.into(),
497	    )
498	    .map_err(|e| {
499	        tracing::error!(error = %e, "failed to create service-auth Bearer client");
500	        MigrationError::AccountCreationFailed {
501	            message: "failed to create Bearer client".to_string(),
502	        }
503	    })?;
504	
505	    // 4. Create account migration (deactivated account)
506	    tracing::info!(
507	        did = %did,
508	        handle = %handle,
509	        "creating destination account (deactivated)"
510	    );
511	
512	    let req = crate::pds_client::CreateAccountMigrationRequest {
513	        handle: handle.into(),
514	        email: email.into(),
515	        did: did.into(),
516	        invite_code,
517	    };
518	
519	    match crate::pds_client::create_account_migration(&sa_client, &req).await {
520	        Ok(resp) => {
521	            // 5. Build destination Bearer client from the returned session tokens.
522	            let dest_client =
523	                OAuthClient::new_bearer(resp.access_jwt, resp.refresh_jwt, dest_pds_url.into())
524	                    .map_err(|e| {
525	                        tracing::error!(error = %e, "failed to create destination Bearer client from response");
526	                        MigrationError::AccountCreationFailed {
527	                            message: "failed to create destination client".to_string(),
528	                        }
529	                    })?;
530	            tracing::info!(did = %did, "destination account created successfully");
531	            Ok(Arc::new(dest_client))
532	        }
533	        // The account already exists at the destination. If we still hold an in-memory dest_client
534	        // we tolerate it (idempotent re-establish — the fast path above usually covers this).
535	        // If not, the destination session was lost (only possible after an app kill wiped in-memory
536	        // state), so the flow must restart from prepare_migration (DESTINATION_CONFLICT).
537	        Err(crate::pds_client::PdsClientError::DidAlreadyExists) => match existing_dest_client {
538	            Some(client) => {
539	                tracing::info!(did = %did, "createAccount 409 but dest_client held; tolerating");
540	                Ok(client)
541	            }
542	            None => {
543	                tracing::error!(did = %did, "createAccount 409 with no dest_client; destination conflict");
544	                Err(MigrationError::DestinationConflict {
545	                    message: "account exists but session was lost (app kill); restart migration"
546	                        .into(),
547	                })
548	            }
549	        },
550	        Err(other) => {
551	            tracing::error!(did = %did, error = %other, "createAccount failed");
552	            Err(MigrationError::AccountCreationFailed {
553	                message: format!("account creation failed: {}", other),
554	            })
555	        }
556	    }
557	}

733	/// Pure core: drain the destination's missing-blob set via cursor pagination.
734	///
735	/// Loops: list_missing_blobs(cursor) → if empty, done; for each blob, fetch from source
736	/// and upload to dest; advance cursor and repeat. Any leg failing aborts with
737	/// BlobTransferFailed WITHOUT advancing the phase, so the whole step is retry-safe.
738	async fn drain_missing_blobs(
739	    pds_client: &crate::pds_client::PdsClient,
740	    dest_client: &OAuthClient,
741	    source_pds_url: &str,
742	    did: &str,
743	) -> Result<(), MigrationError> {
744	    let mut cursor: Option<String> = None;
745	    loop {
746	        let page = crate::pds_client::list_missing_blobs(dest_client, cursor.as_deref())
747	            .await
748	            .map_err(|e| {
749	                tracing::error!(did = %did, error = %e, "list_missing_blobs failed");
750	                MigrationError::BlobTransferFailed {
751	                    message: format!("failed to list missing blobs: {}", e),
752	                }
753	            })?;
754	
755	        // Terminate when page is empty
756	        if page.blobs.is_empty() {
757	            tracing::debug!(did = %did, "blob drain complete: missing set is empty");
758	            return Ok(());
759	        }
760	
761	        // Upload each blob on this page
762	        for blob in &page.blobs {
763	            tracing::debug!(did = %did, cid = %blob.cid, "fetching blob from source");
764	            let bytes = pds_client
765	                .fetch_blob(source_pds_url, did, &blob.cid)
766	                .await
767	                .map_err(|e| {
768	                    tracing::error!(did = %did, cid = %blob.cid, error = %e, "fetch_blob failed");
769	                    MigrationError::BlobTransferFailed {
770	                        message: format!("failed to fetch blob {}: {}", blob.cid, e),
771	                    }
772	                })?;
773	
774	            tracing::debug!(did = %did, cid = %blob.cid, bytes_len = %bytes.len(), "uploading blob to destination");
775	            crate::pds_client::upload_blob(dest_client, "application/octet-stream", bytes)
776	                .await
777	                .map_err(|e| {
778	                    tracing::error!(did = %did, cid = %blob.cid, error = %e, "upload_blob failed");
779	                    MigrationError::BlobTransferFailed {
780	                        message: format!("failed to upload blob {}: {}", blob.cid, e),
781	                    }
782	                })?;
783	        }
784	
785	        // Walk pages: advance cursor or loop with None (will re-list and see empty on success)
786	        cursor = page.cursor;
787	    }
788	}

content.text: Let me look at the test MigrationState construction and the e2e test around line 2883 and 3270.

I now have a complete picture. Let me mark this as the implementation chapter and start editing.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The root cause is a **non-idempotent side effect guarded by `.take()`**: taking the signed op under the lock prevents a double-POST but *orphans* the op if the response is lost after plc.directory commits. The fix inverts the strategy — instead of destroying the op to prevent re-submission, **keep it parked and reconcile the landed-state before every POST**. PLC's `prev`-chaining already makes a stale re-POST impossible (the head moved), so `.take()` was never the only thing preventing double-apply — it was just the crudest. The op's **CID** (content-address that plc.directory assigns) is the exact key to detect landing in the audit log.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

mcp-test:

# Shared gate list both `ci` variants run before their clippy/test/audit/deny tail.
# Adding a check here covers `just ci` (macOS/full) and `just ci-pds` (Linux) at once —
# the old design re-stated all twelve checks in each, so a gate added to one and
# forgotten in the other was a silent gap.
checks: fmt-check lock-check bruno-check font-check cap-check ios-paths-check swift-rs-check ios-template-check

# Run the full CI pipeline locally (all crates; use on macOS where the iOS app builds)
ci: checks clippy test audit deny

# CI gate for the Linux pds pipeline (GitHub Actions, .github/workflows/ci.yml). Excludes the

# absent in CI; the mobile apps are built and checked via `just ios-*` / `just admin-*` on macOS.

    cargo clippy --workspace --exclude identity-wallet --exclude admin-companion --all-targets -- -D warnings
    cargo test --workspace --exclude identity-wallet --exclude admin-companion
    just audit
    just deny

This is an internal resilience change — the frontend IPC contract (`SignedMigrationOp`, `submitMigrationOp`) is unchanged, so no CLAUDE.md contract updates are needed. fix(wallet): reconcile ambiguous/lost-response PLC submit before retry (MM-355)

The outbound-migration identity-leg submit took the signed op under the lock
and cleared migration_state only after a confirmed 200. If plc.directory
committed the op but the HTTP response was lost (mobile network drop), the
wallet dead-ended: signed_op was gone but the state was never cleared, so a
retry hit terminal MIGRATION_NOT_READY and finalizeMigration's `state == None`
gate could not proceed — the migration stranded despite the account being fine.

Reconcile the op's landed-state around the submit instead:
- Keep the signed op (and its CID) parked — clone, don't take.
- Reconcile-first: if a non-nullified audit-log entry already carries the op's
  CID, finalize from current state without re-POSTing.
- Otherwise POST; on failure reconcile once more (a lost response can hide a
  committed op) before surfacing the retryable error.

Double-apply stays impossible: reconcile-first suppresses a re-POST after a
landing, and PLC prev-chaining rejects a stale re-POST, so .take() is no longer
needed as the anti-double-post guard. The op's CID (the content-address
plc.directory assigns) is threaded from build_did_plc_rotation_op through
MigrationState as the reconciliation key.

The frontend retry already re-invokes submitMigrationOp; it is now idempotent,
so the stranded-migration path is gone (comments updated to match). Adds pure
landed/not-landed tests plus mock-plc.directory reconcile-first, happy-path, and
error-propagation tests.
EOF

cd /Users/jacob.zweifel/workspace/malpercio-dev/ezpds && gh pr create --repo malpercio-dev/ezpds --base main --head claude/mm-355-migration-submit-resilience-894966 --title "fix(wallet): reconcile ambiguous/lost-response PLC submit before retry (MM-355)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

The outbound-migration identity-leg submit (`submit_migration_op_cmd`) was not resilient to an **ambiguous / lost-response** PLC submission. A did:plc op is `prev`-chained and non-idempotent, so the command `.take()`-ed the signed op under the lock (to prevent a double-POST) and cleared `migration_state` only *after* a confirmed 200.

If plc.directory committed the op but the HTTP response was lost (mobile network drop), the wallet dead-ended:

- `migration_state = Some { signed_op: None }` — the op was taken but state was never cleared.
- The frontend saw a transport error, so its `submitted` flag stayed `false`.
- On retry, `approve()` re-called `submitMigrationOp` → the backend found `signed_op == None` → returned terminal `MIGRATION_NOT_READY`.
- `finalizeMigration` also couldn't proceed — its gate requires `migration_state == None`, but it was `Some`.

The account was never broken (the identity op landed, so the DID points at the destination), but the in-app migration stranded and needed manual recovery.

## Fix

Reconcile the op's landed-state around the submit instead of destroying the op to prevent a re-POST:

- **Keep the signed op parked** (clone, don't `take`) along with its **CID** — the content-address plc.directory assigns the op once it lands — threaded from `build_did_plc_rotation_op` through `MigrationState`.
- **Reconcile-first**: if a non-nullified audit-log entry already carries the op's CID, finalize from current state without re-POSTing.
- Otherwise **POST**; on failure **reconcile once more** (a lost response can hide a committed op) before surfacing the retryable error.
- The op is cleared from state only once it is confirmed landed.

Double-apply stays impossible: reconcile-first suppresses a re-POST after a landing, and PLC `prev`-chaining rejects a stale re-POST even under a concurrent race — so the old `.take()` anti-double-post guard is no longer needed.

The frontend retry already re-invokes `submitMigrationOp`; it is now idempotent, so the stranded-migration path is gone. The stale comments claiming re-submit "fails terminally" were updated to describe the new reconcile-on-retry behavior. No change to the MM-354 cutover ordering.

## Tests

- Pure `migration_op_landed` unit tests: non-nullified match, absent, and nullified-match-ignored.
- Mock-`plc.directory` (`#[ignore]`, socket-binding — repo convention) tests for `submit_migration_op_reconciling`: reconcile-first skips the POST when already landed, happy-path POSTs when not landed, and a rejected op that didn't land surfaces the error (not masked). All three verified passing against a live mock (`-- --ignored`).
- `cargo clippy -p identity-wallet --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; full suite `373 passed; 0 failed`.

Closes MM-355.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -5

{"id":"MM-355","title":"Migration identity-leg submit: reconcile ambiguous/lost-response PLC submit before retry","description":"## Problem

The outbound-migration identity-leg submit (`migrate::submit_migration_op_cmd`) is not resilient to an **ambiguous / lost-response** PLC submission. Because a PLC operation is `prev`-chained and non-idempotent, `submit_migration_op_cmd` `.take()`s the signed op under the lock (to prevent a double-POST) and clears `migration_state` only *after* a confirmed 200.

If [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) commits the op but the HTTP response is lost (mobile network drop), the wallet lands in a dead-end state:

* `migration_state = Some { signed_op: None }` (op was taken, but state not cleared because no success was observed).
* The frontend (`MigrationReviewScreen.svelte`) sees a transport error, so its `submitted` flag stays `false`.
* On retry, `approve()` re-calls `submitMigrationOp` → `submit_migration_op_cmd` finds `signed_op == None` → returns terminal `MIGRATION_NOT_READY` ("no signed op; build the migration operation first").
* `finalizeMigration` also can't proceed: its gate requires `migration_state == None`, but it's `Some`.

The account is **not** broken (the source is still active and the identity op did land, so the DID points at the destination), but the in-app migration is stranded and needs manual recovery.

This is **pre-existing** (the pre-<issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue> `approve()` had the same re-submit-on-retry behavior) and is upstream of the <issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue> cutover, so it was deliberately left out of that PR (see <pull-request id="3505a4f2-76ee-49d6-a809-2de4d00f96dc" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/review/featwallet-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source-66d203513560">malpercio-dev/ezpds#235</pull-request> — CodeRabbit thread on `MigrationReviewScreen.svelte`).

## Proposed fix

Reconcile the identity op's landed-state before deciding to re-submit vs. proceed:

* On a submit failure (or on entry to `submit_migration_op_cmd` with an already-taken `signed_op`), fetch the DID's PLC audit log and check whether the migration op already landed (current `atproto_pds` service == destination, or the latest non-nullified op matches the built op).
* If **landed** → clear `migration_state`, return the equivalent `ClaimResult`, and let the flow continue to `finalizeMigration` (which is now idempotent per <issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue>).
* If **not landed** → the op can be safely rebuilt (`build_migration_op`) and re-submitted, since `prev` is unchanged.
* Wire the frontend retry to this reconciliation rather than blindly re-invoking `submitMigrationOp`.

Sibling to <issue id="91456924-d043-4164-baa8-112e1ff1e865" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-299/migration-mode-createaccount-is-not-resumable-a-mid-flight-failure">MM-299</issue> (migration-mode createAccount resumability). Add mock tests for the landed/not-landed reconciliation branches.

## Non-goals

* No change to the <issue id="c241fe54-9a79-4403-a428-8e4fdc64be89" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-354/migration-cutover-persist-destination-sovereign-session-before-source">MM-354</issue> cutover ordering (activate → sovereign session → persist → deactivate → Finalized), which already handles its own idempotent retry.","priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-355/migration-identity-leg-submit-reconcile-ambiguouslost-response-plc","gitBranchName":"malpercio/mm-355-migration-identity-leg-submit-reconcile-ambiguouslost","createdAt":"2026-07-14T00:15:55.161Z","updatedAt":"2026-07-14T21:38:52.567Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":"2026-07-14T21:15:47.557Z","canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"In Review","statusType":"started","labels":["Wave 3: Key Sovereignty","Mobile: Identity Wallet","Bug"],"attachments":[{"id":"2f794855-a176-4264-b92c-80775d03c281","title":"fix(wallet): reconcile ambiguous/lost-response PLC submit before retry (MM-355)","subtitle":null,"url":"https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/265"}],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Malpercio","createdById":"5af222b1-08a6-485f-b6e6-26ff3fcff509","assignee":"Malpercio","assigneeId":"5af222b1-08a6-485f-b6e6-26ff3fcff509","project":"ezpds","projectId":"2b0ca2e9-cd15-4ab2-8a55-1efad70eb8a1","parentId":"MM-306","team":"Mal's Machinations","teamId":"9278a20f-995f-49ab-b09d-a340fdcaea72"}

Done. MM-355 is complete, verified, and shipped.

## Summary

The bug was a **non-idempotent side effect protected by the wrong guard**. `submit_migration_op_cmd` `.take()`-ed the signed PLC op to prevent a double-POST, but if plc.directory committed the op and the HTTP *response* was lost, the op was gone and `migration_state` was never cleared — a permanent dead-end (retry → terminal `MIGRATION_NOT_READY`; `finalizeMigration` blocked because state was `Some`, not `None`).

### The fix — reconcile instead of destroy

- **Keep the op parked** (clone, don't `take`) with its **CID** — the content-address plc.directory assigns, threaded from `build_did_plc_rotation_op` → `SignedMigrationOp` → `MigrationState`.
- **Reconcile-first**: if a non-nullified audit-log entry already carries the op's CID, finalize from current state without re-POSTing.
- **POST**, then **reconcile-after** on failure — a lost response can hide a committed op — before surfacing the retryable error.
- Clear state only once the op is confirmed landed.

`.take()` is no longer the anti-double-post guard: reconcile-first suppresses re-POST after a landing, and PLC `prev`-chaining rejects a stale re-POST even under a race. The frontend retry already re-invokes `submitMigrationOp`, which is now idempotent — the stranded-migration path is gone (stale comments updated).

### Verification

- **373 passed, 0 failed**; `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `rustfmt --check` clean.
- New pure `migration_op_landed` tests (match / absent / nullified-ignored) run in CI.
- Three mock-`plc.directory` tests (reconcile-first-skips-POST, happy-path-POSTs, error-not-masked) — **actually executed** with `--ignored`, which caught brittle assertions *and* surfaced a redundant audit-log fetch I then eliminated.

**PR:** [malpercio-dev/ezpds#265](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/265) · Linear MM-355 → **In Review** with the PR linked.

One thing worth flagging: the happy-path submit reads the audit log twice (reconcile-first pre-POST + cache-refresh post-POST). That second read is genuinely necessary (it must reflect the landing), so it's correct, not wasteful — but I documented it explicitly in the test so the call count is intentional rather than accidental.

# Batch PR Review-Comment Triage

Pull every unresolved review thread on the current PR in one command, then triage the batch. The user should never have to paste review comments one at a time.

## Fetch unresolved threads

Determine the PR number for the current branch (`gh pr view --json number -q .number`), then:

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='
query($owner:String!,$repo:String!,$pr:Int!){
  repository(owner:$owner,name:$repo){
    pullRequest(number:$pr){
      reviewThreads(first:100){
        nodes{
          isResolved isOutdated path line
          comments(first:30){nodes{author{login} body url}}
        }
      }
    }
  }
}' -F owner=<owner> -F repo=<repo> -F pr=<number> \
| jq '[.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[]
       | select(.isResolved==false)
       | {path, line, isOutdated,
          comments: [.comments.nodes[] | {author: .author.login, url, body}]}]'
```

Also fetch top-level (non-thread) review bodies and issue comments if the bot posts summaries there:

```bash
gh pr view <number> --json reviews,comments
```

## Triage the batch

For each unresolved thread, classify before fixing anything:

1. **Correctness / security / portability** — verify the claim against the actual code, then fix if real. Automated reviewers assert confidently and are sometimes wrong; refute with evidence when they are.
2. **Legitimate but out of scope** — file a follow-up issue rather than growing the PR.
3. **Pure style nit / preference** — decline with a one-line reason.

Present the full disposition table (thread → classification → action) to the user in ONE message before applying fixes, so they approve the batch rather than each item. Note that every fix-commit re-triggers CI and (for assertive bots like CodeRabbit) a fresh review round that tends to find one more micro-nit — batch fixes into a single commit where possible.

## Resolving threads

After pushing fixes, reply/resolve via:

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='mutation($id:ID!){resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:$id}){thread{isResolved}}}' -F id=<threadId>
```

(Include `id` in the reviewThreads query above if you plan to resolve threads programmatically.)

Even though the migration flow is sequential on the frontend, adding the op_cid check is a cheap defensive improvement that ensures we only clear the exact state we submitted. The reconciliation paths work correctly with this guard — if the operation already landed, my held op_cid matches the state's, so the clear fires as expected. # Obsign (identity-wallet) Mobile App

Last verified: 2026-07-08
Last updated: 2026-07-14

## Purpose

Tauri v2 iOS application — SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 frontend running in a native WKWebView, communicating with a Rust backend exclusively through Tauri's IPC bridge. First frontend code in the repository.

## Contracts

### Frontend (SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5)

**Exposes:**
- `src/lib/ipc/` — per-domain typed wrappers for all Tauri IPC commands, re-exported from `src/lib/ipc/index.ts`; import from `$lib/ipc` instead of calling `invoke()` directly. Exports: `createAccount()`, `performDIDCeremony()`, `registerHandle()`, `getAvailableUserDomains()`, `registerCreatedIdentity()`, `startOAuthFlow()`, `getPdsUrl()`, `savePdsUrl()`, `getAppearancePreference()`, `setAppearancePreference()`, `resolveIdentity()`, `authenticateSourcePds()`, `requestClaimVerification()`, `signAndVerifyClaim()`, `submitClaim()`, `listIdentities()`, `getStoredDidDoc()`, `getDeviceKeyId()`, `checkIdentityStatus()`, `buildRecoveryOverride()`, `submitRecoveryOverride()`, and their associated types (`CreateAccountResult`, `CreateAccountError`, `DIDCeremonyResult`, `DIDCeremonyError`, `RegisterHandleResult`, `RegisterHandleError`, `RegisterIdentityError`, `OAuthError`, `PdsConfigError`, `AppearancePreference`, `AppearanceError`, `IdentityInfo`, `VerifiedClaimOp`, `OpDiff`, `ServiceChange`, `ClaimResult`, `ResolveError`, `ClaimError`, `IdentityStoreError`, `UnauthorizedChange`, `IdentityStatus`, `SignedRecoveryOp`, `RecoveryError`, `SignedMigrationOp`, `MigrateError`) and migration wrappers (`buildMigrationOp()`, `submitMigrationOp()`) and outbound-migration orchestrator wrappers (`prepareMigration()`, `authenticateMigrationSource()`, `createDestinationAccount()`, `transferRepo()`, `transferBlobs()`, `transferPreferences()`, `verifyImport()`, `armIdentityLeg()`, `finalizeMigration()`) with types (`AccountStatus`, `PreparedMigration`, `MigrationError`)
- `src/lib/components/onboarding/` — seventeen onboarding screen components (ModeSelectScreen, PdsConfigScreen, ClaimCodeScreen, EmailScreen, HandleScreen, PasswordScreen, LoadingScreen, DIDCeremonyScreen, DIDSuccessScreen, ShamirBackupScreen, HandleRegistrationScreen, AuthenticatingScreen, IdentityInputScreen, PdsAuthScreen, EmailVerificationScreen, ReviewOperationScreen, ClaimSuccessScreen)
- `src/lib/components/home/` — eight home screen components (IdentityListHome, DIDDocumentScreen, AlertDetailScreen, RecoveryOverrideScreen, MyAgentsScreen, AgentDetailScreen, AgentClaimApprovalScreen, SettingsScreen) plus DIDAvatar utility component (deterministic DID-derived hue circle). MyAgentsScreen is the agent list; AgentDetailScreen is the per-agent sub-view (audit-trail paging + biometric-gated revoke) it renders on selection, its lifetime scoped to that selection
- `src/lib/appearance.ts` — in-app appearance override (System / Light / Dark): `normalizePreference()` / `toColorScheme()` (pure, tested by `appearance.test.ts`), `readLocalMirror()`, `initAppearance()` (launch-time reconcile: re-asserts the localStorage mirror, then reads the Keychain via IPC and lets it win), `setAppearance()` (applies the inline `color-scheme` override on `<html>` instantly, writes the mirror, then persists to the Keychain). The localStorage mirror (key `appearance-preference`) exists only so `src/app.html`'s inline `<head>` script can apply a forced appearance before first paint; the Keychain is the source of truth
- `src/lib/agent-scopes.ts` — plain-language descriptions of granular OAuth scope tokens for the agent-consent surfaces: `describeScope(token)` / `describeScopes(tokens)` return `{ summary, token, elevated }` (the raw token is always shown alongside the human sentence; `account:*`/`identity:*`/full-access grants are flagged `elevated`; an unknown token falls back to showing itself, never a vague label). Tested by `agent-scopes.test.ts`
- `src/lib/deadline.ts` — PLC recovery deadline utilities: `getDeadline(createdAt)` (adds 72h to ISO 8601 timestamp), `getUrgency(deadline)` (returns `'safe'` | `'warning'` | `'critical'` | `'expired'`), `formatCountdown(deadline)` (human-readable `"Xh Ym remaining"`). `Urgency` type exported. Thresholds: expired = 0, critical < 4h, warning < 24h, safe >= 24h
- `src/routes/+page.svelte` — root page: two-flow state machine starting at `mode_select`. **Create flow:** mode_select -> pds_config -> claim_code -> email -> handle -> password (every pre-submit step wires `onback` to the previous step) -> loading -> did_ceremony -> did_success -> shamir_backup -> handle_registration -> complete -> authenticating -> home (after handle_registration succeeds, `finishCreateFlow()` calls `registerCreatedIdentity()` to persist the new identity to `IdentityStore` so it appears in `IdentityListHome` — best-effort, never blocks the flow). **Import flow:** mode_select -> identity_input -> pds_auth -> email_verification -> review_operation -> claim_success -> home. **Home:** home -> identity_detail -> alert_detail -> recovery_override. On mount, checks for existing identities via `listIdentities()` and skips to `home` if any exist. Registers a `visibilitychange` listener that calls `checkIdentityStatus()` when the app returns to foreground while on the `home` step

**Guarantees:**
- SSR is disabled globally (`ssr = false` in `src/routes/+layout.ts`); the frontend is a fully static SPA loaded from disk by WKWebView
- Build output lands in `dist/` (configured via `pages: 'dist'` in `svelte.config.js`)
- Frontend calls Tauri commands only through the `src/lib/ipc/` modules (imported from `$lib/ipc`) — no raw `invoke()` calls in page components
- PDS error codes from `create_account` are mapped back to the originating screen (e.g. EXPIRED_CODE -> claim_code step, EMAIL_TAKEN -> email step)

**Expects:**
- `pnpm install` has been run in `apps/identity-wallet/`
- Node.js 22.x is in PATH (provided by the Nix dev shell)

### Rust Backend (src-tauri/)

**Exposes:**
- `src/lib.rs::create_account(claim_code, email, handle) -> Result<CreateAccountResult, CreateAccountError>` — Tauri IPC command: gets or creates device key via `device_key::get_or_create()`, POSTs to PDS `/v1/accounts/mobile`, stores tokens in Keychain on success
- `src/lib.rs::perform_did_ceremony(handle: String, password: String) -> Result<DIDCeremonyResult, DIDCeremonyError>` — Tauri IPC command: fetches PDS signing key (GET /v1/pds/keys), builds signed did:plc genesis op via `crypto::build_did_plc_genesis_op_with_external_signer` using device key as signer, POSTs genesis op + password to PDS (POST /v1/dids with Bearer token), persists DID + upgraded session token + Share 1 in Keychain, returns `{ did, share3 }` to frontend
- `src/lib.rs::{prepare_did_web_ceremony,complete_did_web_ceremony}` — did:web sibling ceremony: obtains the same device key and pending account's reserved repo key, lets the frontend compose/export the reviewed `did.json`, then submits it to `POST /v1/dids` only after it is externally resolvable. Completion persists the upgraded session and unchanged Shamir Share 1; managed-hosting selection then opts the account into `/v1/did-web/hosting`.
- `src/oauth.rs` — OAuth PKCE client module: `AppState` (pending_login + oauth_session mutexes + custos_client OnceLock + pds_client + claim_state + recovery_state + migration_state + orchestration_state; both source logins — the claim flow and the outbound migration — are password-based `createSession`, so neither parks OAuth state — see `claim::authenticate_source_pds` / `migration_orchestrator::authenticate_migration_source`), `OAuthSession` (access/refresh/expiry/nonce), `DPoPKeypair` (P-256, persisted in Keychain), `OAuthError` enum, PKCE utilities (verifier + S256 challenge), `OAuthPrepared` (the `{authUrl, callbackScheme}` returned to the frontend), `prepare_oauth_flow` + `complete_oauth_flow` (the create-flow login split around the in-app auth session: prepare does DPoP keygen/PKCE/PAR → authorize URL and parks the verifier+CSRF in `pending_login`; complete validates the callback URL + does the token exchange), `parse_callback_url` (shared callback-URL parser, `pub(crate)`); `AppState::pds_client()` accessor exposes `PdsClient` for claim flow commands
- `src/claim.rs` — PLC rotation key claim flow module (5 Tauri IPC commands): `resolve_identity(handle_or_did) -> Result<IdentityInfo, ResolveError>` (resolves handle/DID to identity info via plc.directory, stores ClaimState), `authenticate_source_pds(did, identifier, password, auth_factor_token?) -> Result<(), ClaimError>` (**password `createSession`** against the source PDS → full-session Bearer `OAuthClient` stored in ClaimState; the next steps are PLC/identity ops that no OAuth `transition:generic` token can drive, so a full session is required — ADR-0021/MM-289; the password is used once and never stored. An email-2FA account returns `TwoFactorRequired` on the token-less attempt — the PDS emails a code and the UI re-invokes with `auth_factor_token`), `request_claim_verification(did) -> Result<(), ClaimError>` (calls `requestPlcOperationSignature` XRPC on old PDS to trigger email verification), `sign_and_verify_claim(did, token) -> Result<VerifiedClaimOp, ClaimError>` (calls `getRecommendedDidCredentials` and `signPlcOperation` on old PDS, fetches audit log, verifies signature + 4-point local checks, stores signed op in ClaimState), `submit_claim(did) -> Result<ClaimResult, ClaimError>` (POSTs signed op to plc.directory, persists identity to IdentityStore, clears ClaimState). Types: `IdentityInfo`, `VerifiedClaimOp`, `OpDiff`, `ServiceChange`, `ClaimResult`, `ClaimState`. Error enums: `ResolveError` (HANDLE_NOT_FOUND, DID_NOT_FOUND, PDS_UNREACHABLE, NETWORK_ERROR), `ClaimError` (INVALID_TOKEN, VERIFICATION_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, UNAUTHORIZED, SOURCE_AUTH_FAILED, TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED, ACCOUNT_MISMATCH, INSECURE_SOURCE_URL, INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE, RATE_LIMITED, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR)

Methods: `get(path)`, `post(path, body)` (JSON), `post_no_body(path)` (zero bytes, no `Content-Type` — for no-input XRPC procedures like `requestPlcOperationSignature`/`activateAccount`, whose lexicons define no input; a spec-strict PDS rejects any body — MM-291), `post_bytes(path, content_type, body)` (raw byte body — CAR repo import + blob upload)

Public API: `get_or_create() -> Result<DevicePublicKey, DeviceKeyError>` (idempotent), `sign(data) -> Result<Vec<u8>, DeviceKeyError>`. Exposes `pub(crate)` account-name consts `DEVICE_KEY_PRIV_ACCOUNT` / `DEVICE_KEY_PUB_ACCOUNT` / `DEVICE_KEY_APP_LABEL_ACCOUNT` (single source of truth for the global device-key Keychain accounts; copied into per-DID slots by `IdentityStore::adopt_global_device_key`)
